Avenge

/uh-VENJ/ - rhymes with revenge · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Avenge means to get revenge for a wrong done to oneself or another.

The colony's lone survivor spends the sequel avenging her crew, hunting the saboteur across three star systems.

Worked Example

The deposed duchess waited twenty years to avenge her exile, returning at the head of an army of the very miners her rival had starved.

Avenge is not simple payback: it answers a real wrong, often on someone else's behalf, and claims justice while it does. You retaliate for a shove; you avenge a betrayal, a ruin, a death — the word asks the wrong to be worthy of it.

How Avenge Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

retaliate

retaliate: strike back in kind, often for a smaller offense

requite

requite: a formal word for repaying treatment, good or ill

Antonyms

pardon

pardon: formally release someone from punishment

forgive

forgive: let go of a wrong without repayment

How Strong Is It? — complain → retaliate → avenge

complain vs. avenge

complain vs. avenge: Complaining answers a wrong with words only — far weaker than avenging it.

retaliate vs. avenge

retaliate vs. avenge: Retaliate strikes back in kind, tit for tat, but it stops short of avenge, which claims full justice for a serious wrong.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: to (a form of ad-)

Root — venge

Root — venge: to claim justice, punish (Latin vindicare)

Put it together

Put it together: A- (to) + venge (to claim justice) = to claim justice for a wrong. Latin vindicare meant to lay legal claim, and avenge keeps that idea: revenge at its grandest poses as justice — a wrong repaid in full and on the record.

Use the root in a new word: vengeance

Use the root in a new word: vengeance: The old ballad promises vengeance — payback claimed in full — for the burned village.

Word Choice

literary / elevated

Avenge claims justice for a real wrong, often on another's behalf — a queen avenges her father; you merely get even over a parking spot. For tit-for-tat answers, retaliate is the honest word; avenge dignifies the payback, so spend it only where the wrong has weight.
